**Bangla Voice Clock** (বাংলা ভয়েস ক্লক) 1.0.0 is the first stable version: a free clock for macOS, Windows and Linux that says the time aloud in Bangla.

## New

- **Noto Sans Bengali.** All text in the window is now set in Google's Noto Sans Bengali, in Bangla and English alike.
- **Tidier English labels.** The interval buttons read **15 min**, **30 min** and **1 hour**, and the appearance choice reads **System**, so every label fits its button.

## Everything in 1.0

- Announces the time every 15, 30 or 60 minutes, by the minute (সকাল দশটা বেজে সাত মিনিট) or the traditional way (সকাল সোয়া দশটা), with or without বেজে.
- Two voices: **Areeba AI**, with a Bangladeshi accent, and the **Classic (1998)** voice.
- Quiet hours to the minute, a talking timer, a chime, and a choice of speaker or headphones.
- Lives in the menu bar, the system tray or the GNOME top bar, with the time beside its icon if you like.
- A Bangla or English window, in light or dark.

## Download

| | |
|---|---|
| **macOS** 12 or later, one universal app for Apple Silicon and Intel | `BanglaVoiceClock-v1.0.0-macos.dmg`: open it and drag **Bangla Voice Clock** onto **Applications**. It isn't signed yet: the first time, if macOS won't open it, go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and choose **Open Anyway**. Or use Homebrew: `brew install --cask saifulmd0/tap/bangla-voice-clock`. |
| **Windows** 10 or later (64-bit) | `BanglaVoiceClock-v1.0.0-windows-setup.exe`. SmartScreen may warn about an unknown publisher: choose **More info → Run anyway**. Or `BanglaVoiceClock-v1.0.0-windows-portable.zip`, which runs from any folder. On 0.3.0 or later, the app offers this update itself. |
| **Ubuntu, Debian, Mint** (64-bit) | `BanglaVoiceClock-v1.0.0-linux-amd64.deb`: run `sudo apt install ./BanglaVoiceClock-v1.0.0-linux-amd64.deb`, which also installs the top-bar extension. |
| **Any Linux** with Flatpak | `BanglaVoiceClock-v1.0.0-linux.flatpak`: run `flatpak install --user ./BanglaVoiceClock-v1.0.0-linux.flatpak`. |
| **Any Linux**, no install | `BanglaVoiceClock-v1.0.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`: extract it and run `bangla-voice-clock/bangla-voice-clock`. |

## Known limits

- The macOS and Windows downloads are not code-signed yet.
- The Linux version is 64-bit Intel/AMD only for now.
- An AppIndicator extension installed after you logged in starts at the next login.
